Name: Travellers Tavern
Author: zebramodder
Description:
[center][size=6][b]Traveller's Tavern[/b][/size]
[size=4]Build a tavern on your farm. Pour drinks, cook for travelers and villagers, hire staff, take bookings and grow your reputation, with villager stories, food trends, a food critic, achievements, a guestbook and more. Everything is explained in an in-game guidebook.[/size][/center]
[center][/center]
[center][size=4][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54185/54185-1792705695-1091857435.png[/img][/size][/center]

[line]

[size=5][font=Arial][b]What is this?[/b][/font][/size]
Travellers Tavern gives you a tavern you can build from Robin, free and from day one. Flip the sign to OPEN in the evening and guests start walking in: out-of-towners from all over Ferngill, and your own neighbors on their days off.

Take their orders, pour drinks at the tap, cook in the tavern kitchen, keep the tables clean, and earn tips, reputation and friendship. As your reputation grows, so does everything else: new recipes, staff, upgrades, weddings booked in your hall, a food critic in the paper and stories from the regulars at the bar.

You don't need to read all of this page first. Everything is explained in-game in the [b]Tavern Guidebook[/b] on the office computer.

[line]

[b][size=6]Mod Highlights[/size][/b]

[b][size=5]Run the bar[/size][/b]
[size=4][b][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54185/54185-1792630582-187300180.png[/img][/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Pour it right.[/b] A quick pouring minigame for wine, beer, pale ale, mead, juice and coffee. Land it in the gold band for double tips.[/*]
[*][b]A real tavern kitchen.[/b] An unlimited fridge, a cooking station that pulls the ingredients for you, and a heater that keeps dishes hot.[/*]
[*][b]An honest menu.[/b] Guests only order drinks you have on tap and dishes you know how to cook.[/*]
[*][b]Plating.[/b] Premium dishes get a short presentation step for a quality bonus.[/*]
[*][b]Seasonal menus.[/b] In-season dishes earn more, and out-of-season imports impress guests.[/*]
[/list][b][size=5]Your guests[/size][/b]
[size=4][b][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54185/54185-1792630601-2052958392.png[/img][/b][/size]
[size=4][b][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54185/54185-1792630608-1662914773.png[/img][/b][/size]

[size=3]Every save gets its own crowd of 24 travelers, each with their own look, hometown, favorite foods and a quirk that changes how they order, wait and tip. These are the regulars from our test farm. Your valley will get different faces, but you'll know the types. [/size]

[list]
[*][b]Travelers with their own faces.[/b] 24 out-of-towners, each with a unique look, name and hometown, built from your own game's character creator.[/*]
[*][b]Villagers drop by[/b] on their days off and order what they'd love as a gift. Serve a favorite for extra friendship and a big tip.[/*]
[*][b]Regulars with stories.[/b] Eight villagers have tavern-only scenes that unfold as your friendship grows. Pam has opinions on your ale, Gus becomes a rival or a mentor, and Shane may ask for your help cutting back.[/*]
[*][b]Reviews and complaints.[/b] Guests pin reviews to a cork board, and now and then someone asks to speak to whoever's in charge.[/*]
[*][b]Solo diners, couples and parties.[/b] Patience bars, messes to clean, and guests who stay for darts or pool.[/*]
[/list][b][size=5]Grow your business[/size][/b]
[size=4][b][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54185/54185-1792630626-134618773.png[/img][/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Reputation and perks.[/b] Ten levels and a perk tree with three branches.[/*]
[*][b]The office computer.[/b] Culinary classes (20 new dishes), hiring staff, group bookings (weddings, birthdays and the Adventurer's Guild), menu costing with food cost percentages, a collection log, achievements and the full guidebook.[/*]
[*][b]Upgrades from Robin.[/b] The Grand Tavern expansion, plus signposts and billboards around town.[/*]
[*][b]A living town.[/b] Food trends (a spicy food craze, Harvey's health kick and more), an unannounced food critic who reviews you in the paper, and a traveling merchant who trades rare ingredients for a meal on the house.[/*]
[/list][b][size=5]Make it yours[/size][/b]
[size=4][b][img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/54185/54185-1792630638-1115991613.png[/img][/b][/size]

[list]
[*][b]Furnish it[/b] with your own tables, chairs and decor. Comfort means bigger tips.[/*]
[*][b]Name it[/b] and design its sign, painted right onto the building.[/*]
[*][b]Little touches:[/b] a seasonal exterior, a tavern cat or dog, darts, pool and board games, and a guestbook that fills up with villagers' signatures, doodles and inside jokes.[/*]
[*][b]A secret.[/b] Long ago, another tavern stood on your farm...[/*]
[/list][line]

[size=5][b]Requirements[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2400]SMAPI[/url] 4.0 or newer (tested with 4.5.2)[/*]
[*]Stardew Valley 1.6.15 on PC[/*]
[/list]No other mods are needed.

[size=5][b]Installation[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2400]SMAPI[/url] if you haven't already.[/*]
[*]Download this mod and unzip it into your [b]Stardew Valley/Mods[/b] folder. You should end up with [b]Mods/TravellersTavern/manifest.json[/b].[/*]
[*]Launch the game through SMAPI.[/*]
[/list]It works with new and existing saves.

[line]

[size=5][b]Getting started[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*][b]Build the Tavern.[/b] Ask Robin. It's free, needs no materials and goes up instantly.[/*]
[*][b]Look around inside.[/b] The tap, heating station, fridge, cooking station, Open/Closed sign, review board, guestbook and an office door are already set up for you.[/*]
[*][b]Add seating.[/b] Place your own tables with chairs next to them. Every chair touching a table is a seat. Bar counter pieces and stools can be crafted, or bought from [i]Tavern Supplies[/i] on the office laptop.[/*]
[*][b]Stock up.[/b] Put drinks (wine, beer, pale ale, mead, juice, coffee) in the tap. Cook dishes at the cooking station; they go into the heater to stay hot.[/*]
[*][b]Open up.[/b] The sign starts on CLOSED every morning. Flip it to OPEN, and from 5pm guests start arriving.[/*]
[*][b]Serve.[/b] Pour the drink or take the hot dish, then right-click the guest while holding it.[/*]
[*][b]Tidy up.[/b] Right-click tables to clear messes. Last orders are at 11pm and you close at midnight, with a ledger of the night.[/*]
[*][b]Learn the rest as you go.[/b] Open the [b]Tavern Guidebook[/b] on the office computer whenever you're curious.[/*]
[/list][b]Tip:[/b] early on, your menu is small. Every cooked dish you buy from a shop teaches you its recipe, and culinary classes on the office laptop add 20 more.

[line]

[size=5][b]Configuration[/b][/size]
A [b]config.json[/b] file appears in the mod folder after your first launch. Some handy settings:
[list]
[*][b]OpenTime / CloseTime / LastOrdersTime[/b]: opening hours (default 1700 / 2400 / 2300).[/*]
[*][b]PatienceMinutes[/b]: how long guests wait before walking out (default 70).[/*]
[*][b]BasePriceMultiplier[/b]: menu prices compared with shop prices (default 1.4).[/*]
[*][b]VillagerVisits, VillagerVisitChance, NeverVisit, DaysOff[/b]: who visits and when.[/*]
[*][b]SeasonalMenus[/b]: seasonal pricing on or off.[/*]
[*][b]FarmWalkIns[/b]: guests walking across the farm into your tavern while you're outside.[/*]
[*][b]MerchantVisits[/b]: the traveling merchant's cart-day visits.[/*]
[*][b]ComplaintChance, ReviewChance[/b]: how often guests complain or leave reviews.[/*]
[*][b]RowdyGuests[/b]: rowdy troublemakers (off by default).[/*]
[/list][line]

[size=5][b]Compatibility[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Single-player.[/b] Multiplayer isn't supported yet.[/*]
[*][b]No game files are replaced.[/b] Everything is added through SMAPI.[/*]
[*]It should work alongside most mods. Mods that heavily change Robin's carpenter menu haven't been tested with it.[/*]
[/list][size=5][b]Uninstalling[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Back up your save.[/*]
[*]Have Robin demolish the Tavern.[/*]
[*]Sell or remove the mod's items (its dishes, stations and furniture) from your inventory and chests.[/*]
[*]Delete the [b]TravellersTavern[/b] folder from Mods.[/*]
[/list]If you skip steps 2 and 3, the game will show broken "Error Item"s for anything the mod added.

[line]

[size=5][b]FAQ[/b][/size]

[b]Nobody is coming in![/b]
[spoiler]
Check that:
[list]
[*]the sign says OPEN and it's after 5pm[/*]
[*]you have at least one seat (a chair touching a table)[/*]
[*]something is on the menu (a drink in the tap, or a dish you know)[/*]
[*]you're inside the tavern, or on your farm[/*]
[/list]Tonight's expected crowd is on the office computer's Tavern tab. Rain, storms and festivals keep people home.[/spoiler]

[b]Everyone keeps ordering the same thing.[/b]
[spoiler]
Your menu probably only has one or two items. Learn more recipes: every cooked dish you buy from a shop (Gus sells several) teaches you its recipe, and the culinary classes on the office laptop have 20 more.[/spoiler]

[b]A guest won't take what I'm handing them.[/b]
[spoiler]
Drinks have to be poured at the tap, and dishes must come hot from the heating station. Guests also only accept what they ordered (check the bubble over their head).[/spoiler]

[b]Where do I find more recipes, staff, perks or upgrades?[/b]
[spoiler]
Almost everything lives on the office computer: the Tavern tab (perks, staff, bookings, sign, menu costing), Culinary Classes, Tavern Supplies, Achievements and the Collection. Robin handles the Grand Tavern and the town advertising.[/spoiler]

[b]Does it work in multiplayer?[/b]
[spoiler]
Not yet. It's designed and tested for single-player.[/spoiler]

[line]

[size=5][b]Known issues[/b][/size]
This is a first release. Daily service has had the most testing; rarer events (the food critic, cart-day merchant visits and parts of the founding legend) have had less. If something goes wrong, please post a bug report with your SMAPI log from [url=https://smapi.io/log]smapi.io/log[/url].

[list]
[*]Made by rmccr, with the help of an AI coding assistant (Claude by Anthropic).[/*]
[*]All art was made for this mod. The out-of-towners are drawn from your own game's character creator when you load a save, so no game assets are included.[/*]

[*]Built with [url=https://smapi.io]SMAPI[/url] by Pathoschild.[/*]
[/list][size=5][b]Changelog[/b][/size]
[b]0.1.0: First Release[/b]

[b]0.1.1: Mixed Drinks & Bug Fixes[/b]

- New: Cocktail mixing. Buy a Shaker Station (2,500g) from Tavern Supplies on the office laptop, then invent your own cocktails from a base spirit (wine, beer, pale ale or mead) and one or two mixers (honey, coffee or any fruit). Name them, put them on the menu, and shake one when a guest orders it.
- New: Cocktails have a flavor profile (sweet, strong, fruity and bitter), and every guest has a flavor they love and one they can't stand. Villagers also go by their gift tastes. A hit earns a bigger tip; a miss gets "Too sweet!" and no tip. Each recipe keeps score of what guests thought.
- New: Mixologist achievement, for inventing 5 cocktails. Cocktails also appear in Menu Costing.
- Changed: The Heating Station now takes any cooked dish, including ones from your farmhouse kitchen or a shop, not just dishes from the tavern's Cooking Station. Ingredients and artisan goods are still refused.
- Changed: The tavern's corner panel now folds to a single line. Click it (or its arrow) to see everything, and again to fold it. Your choice is remembered.
- Fixed: Long lines in the tavern panel, such as a busy forecast, no longer run past the edge of the box.

[b]0.1.2: New Faces at the Tavern[/b]

- New: out-of-towners rebuilt as 12 kinds of traveler with matching outfits. Each save gets two of each kind.
- New: likes and dislikes. Guests order what they love more often and rarely order what they hate. They tip extra for their favorite, and their tastes carry over to cocktails.
- New: quirks, such as big tippers, night owls, reviewers, game fans and big eaters, plus remarks when they sit down and the Collection hover card.
- Changed: Served counts are stored by slot, so each newcomer inherits the old traveler’s count. Old guestbook entries keep the names they were signed with.
- Fixed: guest names no longer pile up at the bar or cover order bubbles.

[b]0.1.3: Shed Mod Compatibility[/b]

[b]-  Changed:[/b] much more dramatic seasonal fronts.
[list]
[*]Spring: bunting, wisteria and pink shutters.[/*]
[*]Summer: window canopies, paper lanterns and blue shutters.[/*]
[*]Fall: red ivy and jack-o’-lanterns.[/*]
[*]Winter: heavy snow, icicles, a garland, colored lights and a snowman.[/*]
[/list]-  [b]New:[/b] a smoking chimney and a seasonal flag on the roof.
-  [b]Changed:[/b] the Grand Tavern gets a clock tower, green walls, cream trim and a balcony.
-  [b]Changed:[/b] the tavern has its own interior, so shed mods no longer affect it. Existing taverns move over automatically, with the furniture left in place
-  [b]Compatibility:[/b] if a shed mod was making the tavern’s room bigger, it goes back to the normal size, so players should pick up anything placed beyond it before updating.
-  [b]Fixed:[/b] custom signs still sit on the board with the taller fronts.

[b]0.1.4: Food Mod Compatibility[/b]

- New: Drinks from other mods now work. Any artisan good the game marks as a drink can go in the tap: cider, sake, whiskey, lemonade, Green Tea and so on. Guests order them, and you pour them in the minigame like the classic six.
- New: Each new drink gets its own pour: a mug with a foamy head for ales and ciders, a mug for coffee and tea, and a glass for wines, spirits and soft drinks, in the drink's own color.
- New: Any alcoholic drink can be a cocktail base, including other mods' spirits and wines.
- New: Dishes with no recipe anywhere, like other mods' shop food or a bought Piña Colada, can go in the Heating Station and onto the menu.
- Changed: Food trends, guest tastes and Shane's story recognize other mods' drinks: ales and ciders count for Craft Brew Fever, wines for wine lovers, and soft drinks as a swap when Shane is cutting back.
- Changed: Menu Costing estimates the cost of drinks it can't trace back to an ingredient, and the Collection lists every drink you could serve.
